hypothesis: The champion CatBoost model (Run 1: ROC-AUC 0.84974) used default features and saturated at 1000 iterations with mild overfitting (Omega=11.27%). Run 5 telemetry identifies low-signal features (StreamingRatio, DeviceProtection_Yes, Dependents_No, DeviceProtection_No) that add noise. Enabling domain-specific feature synthesis (charge ratios, tenure cohorts, service density, interaction terms) will capture non-linear relationships like tenure-charge interactions and service bundling effects, directly targeting the high false negative rate (46.5%). Pruning the four low-signal features reduces dimensionality. Reducing depth to 5 and increasing L2 leaf regularization to 5.0 will tighten generalization (target Omega ~5-8%), while lowering learning rate to 0.03 with 1500 iterations ensures finer convergence.
mathematical_justification: Run 1 Omega=11.27% indicates mild overfitting; increasing L2 from 3.0 to 5.0 and reducing depth from 6 to 5 reduces model complexity, lowering generalization gap. The learning rate reduction from 0.05 to 0.03 with 50% more iterations (1500 vs 1000) follows the learning curve dynamics: Run 5 showed saturation at 100 iterations for LR, but CatBoost requires more trees; lower LR with more iterations yields better optima. Feature enrichment addresses the PR-AUC deficit (0.66538) by creating high-signal interactions. Dropping four near-zero importance features reduces noise variance.
expected_outcome: ROC-AUC improvement to 0.852-0.855 (+0.002 to +0.005) and PR-AUC to 0.67-0.68 by capturing churn-specific interactions and reducing false negatives.

hypothesis: The premature early stopping at 18.5% of iteration budget (278/1500) with a negative validation loss tail slope (-1e-5) indicates the learning rate (0.03) is too aggressive for the current regularization (L2=5.0) and depth (5), causing the optimizer to overshoot the narrow loss minima. Reducing learning rate to 0.025 with increased iterations (2000) and stronger L2 regularization (7.0) will enable finer convergence. Pruning near-zero importance features (Contract_x_Payment, PhoneService) reduces noise variance. Enabling explicit interaction terms captures non-linear synergies between high-signal features (Contract, MonthlyCharges, InternetService), targeting PR-AUC improvement.
mathematical_justification: Run 6 Omega=7.14% (Generalization Gap=0.0294) shows stable generalization but suboptimal convergence: early stopping utilized only 18.5% of tree budget with negative tail slope, indicating learning rate too high for current curvature. Lowering LR to 0.025 increases effective steps per unit loss reduction by ~20%. Increasing L2 to 7.0 (within suggested 4.0-10.0 bounds) constrains leaf weights further, reducing variance. Depth=5 maintained (within 4-6 bounds) preserves capacity. Pruning 2 low-signal features reduces dimensionality noise. Interaction terms may boost PR-AUC by modeling Contract-MonthlyCharges synergies.
expected_outcome: ROC-AUC > 0.8500 (target +0.0003), PR-AUC > 0.6665 (target +0.0006), Omega ~5-6%, early stopping utilization >40% of iterations, improved calibration (ECE < 0.012).

hypothesis: Enabling domain-specific feature synthesis (charge ratios, tenure cohorts, service density, interaction terms) will capture non-linear churn signals missed by raw features, while dropping near-zero importance features (SeniorCitizen, DeviceProtection) reduces noise. Increasing tree depth to 6 with moderate L2 regularization (5.0) and a slightly higher learning rate (0.03) will exploit the low overfitting index (Omega=5.02%) and negative validation loss tail slope (-1.8e-5) to push ROC-AUC beyond 0.84974. Extending early_stopping_rounds to 100 prevents premature stopping at 18% of iteration budget.
mathematical_justification: Run 7 shows Omega=5.02% (well below 18% overfitting threshold) and a negative tail slope (-0.000018), indicating the model had not fully converged when early stopping triggered at iteration 362/2000. The generalization gap (0.0206) is small, allowing capacity increase. Depth=6 (within suggested 4-6) with l2_leaf_reg=5.0 (within 4-10) balances bias-variance. Learning rate 0.03 (within 0.025-0.05) accelerates convergence while early_stopping_rounds=100 provides patience for the flat loss tail. Feature enrichment targets the 48% false negative rate by creating churn-sensitive interactions (e.g., MonthlyToTotalRatio already 11.2% importance).
expected_outcome: OOF ROC-AUC > 0.8505 and PR-AUC > 0.667 via richer feature representation and better-converged gradient boosting, while maintaining Omega < 10%.

hypothesis: Run 8 telemetry shows premature early stopping at 11.3% of iteration budget (227/2000) with a flat validation loss tail slope (0.000000), indicating learning rate 0.03 is too aggressive and causes the optimizer to settle in a wide, suboptimal basin. Lowering learning rate to 0.02 with increased iterations (3000) will allow finer gradient steps to navigate narrower minima. Increasing L2 leaf regularization to 10.0 (within suggested 6-15 bound) and reducing depth to 5 (within suggested 4-5 bound) will further constrain model complexity, lowering the Overfitting Index (Omega=7.46%) toward the 3-5% sweet spot. Pruning near-zero importance features PhoneService and TenureGroup removes noise. Enabling interaction terms captures non-linear synergies between high-signal features (Contract, InternetService, MonthlyToTotalRatio).
mathematical_justification: Generalization Gap = 0.0306, Omega = 7.46% (stable but above 5% target). Early stopping utilization = 227/2000 = 11.3% << 25%, confirming learning rate too high. Reducing lr to 0.02 increases effective iterations to ~340 (assuming similar early stopping rounds), improving convergence resolution. L2 increase from 5.0 to 10.0 adds stronger leaf weight shrinkage, directly reducing variance. Depth reduction from 6 to 5 decreases tree capacity, aligning with suggested bounds. Feature pruning eliminates two zero-gain features, reducing dimensionality without signal loss. Interaction terms may increase PR-AUC by improving ranking of minority class.
expected_outcome: ROC-AUC improvement to ~0.8515 (+0.0012) and PR-AUC to ~0.670 (+0.0026) by achieving tighter convergence, lower Omega (~5%), and better minority class ranking via interaction terms.

hypothesis: Pruning near-zero importance features (Dependents, DeviceProtection, SeniorCitizen, gender) will reduce input noise and improve generalization given the stable but low Overfitting Index (Omega=6.12%). Increasing L2 regularization to 12.0 (within suggested 6.0-15.0 bounds) combined with a marginally higher learning rate of 0.022 (within 0.02-0.035 bounds) will better utilize the iteration budget (early stopping at only 17.2% of 3000 iterations) to find a sharper validation loss minimum without triggering overfitting. Feature enrichment via charge ratios, tenure cohorts, service density, and interaction terms will inject domain-specific signal to boost minority class discrimination (FNR=46.7%).
mathematical_justification: Run 9 telemetry shows Generalization Gap = 0.0251, Omega = 6.12% (well below 18% overfitting threshold), indicating capacity for increased regularization. Val loss tail slope = -5e-6 (still descending) and early stopping at iteration 516/3000 (17.2%) suggests learning rate 0.02 is slightly too conservative, leaving optimization incomplete. Increasing LR to 0.022 accelerates convergence while L2=12.0 constrains leaf weights to maintain Omega < 10%. Dropping 4 stagnant features (SHAP ~0%) reduces variance. Historical velocity dROC-AUC/dRun = +0.00006 implies diminishing returns; feature engineering targets PR-AUC uplift via better churner ranking.
expected_outcome: OOF ROC-AUC improvement to ~0.8515 (+0.0012) and PR-AUC to ~0.6675 (+0.002) via noise reduction, better optimization dynamics, and enriched feature interactions targeting the 46.7% false negative rate.

hypothesis: The champion model (Run 9) exhibits a low Overfitting Index (Omega=6.12%) but a critically high False Negative Rate (47.4%) and suboptimal PR-AUC (0.6655) relative to ROC-AUC (0.8503), indicating insufficient gradient focus on the minority churn class under 'None' class weighting. Switching to 'SqrtBalanced' class_weight_mode will reweight gradients by sqrt(class frequency), improving recall/PR-AUC without the high variance of full 'Balanced' weighting. Concurrently, pruning near-zero importance features 'Contract_x_Payment' and 'StreamingMovies' reduces noise. Slightly reducing L2 regularization to 8.0 (within suggested bounds 6.0-15.0) exploits the low Omega headroom to capture finer minority-class decision boundaries, while maintaining the optimal learning rate (0.02) and depth (5) confirmed by Run 9's early stopping at 8.3% budget utilization.
mathematical_justification: Run 9 Telemetry: Omega = 6.12% (Val Loss 0.411 - Train Loss 0.384 / Val Loss 0.411), Generalization Gap = 0.027. This is well below the 18% overfitting threshold, providing regularization headroom to decrease l2_leaf_reg from 10.0 to 8.0. FNR = 47.4% at Youden J* (0.29) confirms class imbalance bias. ECE = 0.0113 indicates good calibration, so probability distortion from class weighting will be minimal. Early stopping at iteration 249/3000 (8.3%) with flat tail slope (-3e-6) confirms LR=0.02 is optimal; reducing LR further risks underfitting given fixed iteration budget. Feature Importance: Contract_x_Payment and StreamingMovies contribute negligibly; pruning reduces VC dimension.
expected_outcome: PR-AUC increase to >0.670 (+0.005) via improved minority class gradient weighting (SqrtBalanced) and noise reduction. ROC-AUC maintenance >0.850. FNR reduction to <40%. Omega expected to rise moderately to ~8-10% but remain safely within generalization bounds.

hypothesis: The champion model (Run 9) achieves low overfitting (Omega=6.12%) but suffers from high false negative rate (31.9%) and suboptimal PR-AUC (0.66549). Run 11 telemetry shows premature early stopping at 15.4% of iterations with a near-zero negative tail slope (-3e-6), indicating the learning rate of 0.02 is too conservative to escape shallow local minima. Two features (TotalServices, PhoneService) have near-zero importance and add noise. Enabling interaction terms will capture non-linear synergies between top features (Contract, MonthlyCharges, tenure). Increasing learning rate to 0.025 with stronger L2 (14) and Balanced class weights will accelerate convergence, improve minority class recall, and boost PR-AUC while maintaining generalization.
mathematical_justification: Omega=5.06% (Run 11) and 6.12% (Run 9) are well below the 18% overfitting threshold, providing regularization headroom. Generalization gap = 0.0234 is minimal. Early stopping at 462/3000 iterations with tail slope -3e-6 implies the learning rate 0.02 under-utilizes the iteration budget; increasing to 0.025 (within suggested 0.02-0.035 bounds) should reach a better minimum. PR-AUC lags ROC-AUC by ~0.185; Balanced class weighting directly reweights the loss gradient to penalize false negatives (churners), targeting PR-AUC improvement. Pruning TotalServices and PhoneService reduces dimensionality by 2 noise features. Interaction terms enable multiplicative feature combinations (e.g., Contract*MonthlyCharges) that tree splits approximate inefficiently. Bagging_temperature=0.3 and random_strength=1.0 inject stochastic regularization to improve ensemble diversity without increasing Omega beyond ~10%.
expected_outcome: ROC-AUC > 0.85033 (target 0.8515), PR-AUC > 0.66549 (target 0.668), Omega ~8-10%, false negative rate < 28%, early stopping utilization > 30% of iterations.

hypothesis: Lowering learning rate to 0.017 will delay premature early stopping (currently 13% of iteration budget) allowing convergence to a flatter minimum; increasing L2 to 16.0 and reducing depth to 4 will maintain the healthy generalization gap (Omega=6.88%) while improving calibration (ECE=0.1449); pruning four stagnant features (Contract_x_Payment, Dependents, SeniorCitizen, gender) reduces noise variance; adding subsample=0.85 and bagging_temperature=0.5 introduces stochastic regularization to boost PR-AUC without harming ROC-AUC.

expected_outcome: ROC-AUC > 0.8510 (target +0.0005), PR-AUC > 0.6660 (target +0.0015), ECE < 0.135, early stopping at 20-25% of iterations (600-750), Omega stabilized at 5-7%.

hypothesis: Pruning near-zero importance features (DeviceProtection, StreamingTV, TotalServices, PhoneService) will reduce input noise and improve the signal-to-noise ratio for the dominant features (Contract, MonthlyToTotalRatio, InternetService). Combined with a lower learning rate (0.015) to resolve the narrow loss minima suggested by the flat negative tail slope (-6e-6) and premature early stopping (18.5% budget utilization), this configuration targets a reduction in generalization gap and an improvement in both ROC-AUC (>0.8506) and PR-AUC (>0.666) while maintaining Balanced class weights to suppress the 18.6% False Negative Rate.
mathematical_justification: Run 13 (Depth=4, L2=16, LR=0.017) achieved Omega=6.32% (stable) but ROC-AUC 0.85013 < Champion 0.85058 (Run 12: Depth=5, L2=14, LR=0.025). The diagnostics indicate premature stopping at iteration 555/3000 with a negative tail slope, suggesting the LR=0.017 steps may overshoot the optimal basin. Reducing LR to 0.015 increases effective resolution per iteration. Run 10 (Depth=5, L2=12, LR=0.022, None) scored 0.84990; switching to Balanced weights (proven in Run 12/13 to help PR-AUC/ECE) and lowering LR to 0.015 explores a previously unvisited high-regularization/low-LR corner of the hyperparameter space. expected_outcome: Target OOF ROC-AUC > 0.8506 (beating Run 12 champion) and PR-AUC > 0.666. Expected Omega ~5-6%. Reduced ECE via Balanced weights and cleaner feature set. Early stopping expected later (>1000 iterations) due to lower LR, allowing fuller convergence.
